newsitem.title: UK: IPE to extend Brent futures to 30 months forward.
newsitem.headline: IPE to extend Brent futures to 30 months forward.

text.p: The International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) is planning to extend its flagship Brent futures contract to 30 months forward trading from the current 12 months.
"The IPE is currently planning the extension of the Brent futures contract to 30 months," Lynton Jones, the IPE's chief executive, told an oil conference in London on Tuesday.
"Central to this development is growing interest in the back months from swaps providers and long-term hegders," he added at the annual Oil and Money conference.
He said Brent futures currently trade the equivalent of 50 million barrels per day (bpd). This compares to world oil demand of around 72 million bpd this year.
Jones also said the IPE intends to use its Electronic Trading System for its much delayed gas futures contract.
